title: 'If they hadn't been there, I'd be dead'; Woman recalls attack before police shooting Man beat up her friend, then forced her inside: [ONT Edition]
article: A Whitby single mother of two knew Dave Noble was obsessed with her, but she never expected him to threaten her life, resulting in him being shot dead by Durham police.
"I never wanted this to happen," Susan Wilson sobbed yesterday as she recounted the events that led up to the shooting at her home in Whitby early Saturday.

Wilson, 41, a teacher's evaluator with the Ontario Secondary School Teachers' Federation, was sitting on the front steps of her home having a cigarette with a man she recently began dating when Noble showed up late Friday night and flew into a rage.
"He beat the s--- out of Bill on the lawn and then dragged me into the house," she said, adding Noble "was never violent before."
After attacking Bill, who left after the beating, Wilson said Noble dragged her into the kitchen, where he grabbed a knife and held it to her throat.
"He told me to go and put my pyjamas on," which she did. She managed to dial 911 and told a dispatcher that a man was threatening her with a knife.
"He chased me around the house with the knife and I ran for the door and got outside. He grabbed me from behind and dragged me back inside, holding the knife to my throat," she said.
"He slammed the door and there was a gunshot. Then Dave was lying on the floor. He didn't move and there was blood everywhere," she said.
Earlier that evening, Wilson's 15-year-old son Jesse and her daughter Ellen, 11, had gone to visit their father.
Noble, 42, a former long-haul trucker, had been unemployed since being injured in an accident some time ago.
He did not drink or take drugs but suffered from depression, Wilson said.
The two met last Christmas Eve.
"I've been trying to tell him for weeks and weeks that I didn't want to be in a relationship with him. He kept saying that he loved me to death," she said.
Wilson said Noble has a teenage daughter living in the United States and a son in New Brunswick, and he lived alone in a highrise apartment near Dundas St. W. and Lake Ridge Rd. South.
There is a large bullet hole in the glass panel by the front door from the single shot that struck Noble, killing him instantly just inside the door.
The Special Investigations Unit has been called in to investigate. The agency looks into incidents involving police and civilians that result in serious injury, sexual assault or death.
"My neighbour said he heard Dave shout to the police, 'Just shoot me.' I didn't hear any of that, I was in total shock."
Still traumatized, Wilson believes police had no choice but to shoot.
"They saved my life," she said. "If they hadn't been here, I'd be dead."
